It's October now, time to get the winter wheat in the ground. I've been farming these fields for 30 years — I know every piece of my 31.5 mu. I've got 25 mu of good flat field land where I run the wheat-maize double crop, same as most folks around here. Then I've got 6.5 mu in smaller plots near the house — that's where I grow my zucchini. It's more work, but the cash is better than grain when the market price holds.

**My 25 mu of wheat-maize:**

For the wheat, I'm planting around October 10th. I'm using Jimai 22, an improved variety — costs me about 28 yuan per mu for seed. The extension guy told me 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is the recommended rate now, but I've been using about 16 kg and my yields stay steady around 460 kg per mu. I don't want to mess with what's working. I'll put down 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base — that's about 6 kg each of N, P, and K — then topdress with 22 kg of urea per mu at jointing in early March. That gives me another 10 kg of nitrogen.

I'll irrigate three times: once in late November before the hard freeze, once at jointing in March, and once at heading in late April. Pumping water costs about 30 yuan per mu for the season, so I watch it carefully. If May turns out bone-dry I'll do a fourth, but three usually gets me through. I'll spray herbicide once in early spring — the weeds have been worse the last couple years.

For the maize next June, I plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid right after wheat harvest — probably June 12th or 13th. The turnaround is brutal, sometimes only five or six days, so I hire the combine and get the seed in fast. I'll do light rotary tillage, no time for deep plowing. Base fertilizer of 45 kg compound per mu at planting, then topdress with 18 kg of urea when the maize has six or seven leaves. I might irrigate once or twice in July and August depending on rain. Last year I only watered once and still got nearly 500 kg per mu. Seed is about 48 yuan per mu for the hybrid.

**My 6.5 mu of zucchini:**

I plant in mid-April, after the frost risk is gone. It's my cash crop. I deep plow in March and make raised beds with plastic mulch — keeps the moisture in and the weeds down. Zucchini is hungry: I put down 70 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base, plus some farmyard manure I've saved. Then two side-dressings of urea during peak fruiting. Total about 18 kg N, 6 kg P, and 10 kg K per mu — the extra potassium helps the fruit set.

I irrigate six times because zucchini needs steady moisture, especially once it starts fruiting. I also have to stay on top of pests — aphids and whitefly are the main problems, plus powdery mildew — so I spray both insecticide and fungicide. It's labor-intensive. I do the daily management myself, but in July at peak harvest I hire two people to help pick every day for about two weeks. That's roughly 10 days of hired labor for the season. I expect about 2,500 kg per mu if the weather cooperates. Last year I got 2,200 kg/mu and the collection point paid 1.6 yuan/kg.

**Costs and tradeoffs:**

Total input costs for the year will run me about 18,000 yuan. The wheat is about 300 yuan per mu, the maize about 280 yuan per mu — those are my stable crops. The zucchini runs about 550 yuan per mu with all the fertilizer, sprays, and hired picking labor. It's a lot, but the zucchini should gross over 25,000 yuan if prices hold. My wife works part-time at a garment workshop in town, so we have some off-farm cash, but I'm still careful — fertilizer prices have gone up and I don't buy the premium stuff, just the regular compound from the agricultural supply store. I don't take big risks. I'd rather apply a bit too much fertilizer than too little and lose yield. A bad year hurts more than a good year helps.

My daughter is working in Shijiazhuang now, so it's mostly me and my wife managing things. I hire help for harvest and peak zucchini picking, but I do the day-to-day work myself. At 53, I know my land and my limits. No fancy technology — just solid management built on 30 years of watching what works.
